events.title: Japan Stock Market Has Another Weak Lead
events.description: The Japan stock market has tracked lower in four straight sessions, slumping more than 2,900 points or 4.1 percent in that span. The Nikkei now sits just above the 67,775-point plateau and it's looking at another soft start again on Wednesday.

events.title: KOSPI May Find Support At Key 6,000-Point Level
events.description: The South Korea stock market has finished lower in five straight sessions, plummeting more than 970 points or 14.5 percent along the way. The KOSPI now sits just above the 6,030-point plateau and it's overdue for support on Wednesday.

events.title: China Inflation, Trade Data Due On Wednesday
events.description: China will on Wednesday release September figures for imports, exports, trade balance and consumer prices, highlighting a modest day for Asia-Pacific economic activity.

events.title: Swiss Market Ends Modestly Higher
events.description: The Switzerland market ended modestly higher on Tuesday after holding in positive territory throughout the trading session as lower oil prices and bond yields helped underpin sentiment.

events.title: Major European Markets Fail To Hold Gains, End Marginally Down
events.description:
The major European markets settled slightly down on Tuesday as oil's rebound from lower levels and weakness in the tech sector amid renewed uncertainty about returns on AI investments rendered the mood cautious past mid-afternoon.

The markets started off on a firm note this morning as oil prices fell and bond yields edged lower.

events.title: TSX Up Firmly In Positive Territory; Energy Stocks Rally
events.description: After a strong start, the Canadian market pared some gains Tuesday morning but still remains firmly placed in positive territory with stocks from energy, communications, consumer staples and financials sectors making significant progress up north.

events.title: U.S. Existing Home Sales Unexpectedly Rebound In September
events.description: Existing home sales in the U.S. unexpectedly increased in the month of September, according to a report released by the National Association of Realtors on Tuesday. NAR said existing home sales jumped by 1.5 percent to an annual rate of 3.99 million in September after plunging by 3.2 percent to a downwardly revised rate of 3.93 million in August.

events.title: IMF Raises Global Growth Outlook Despite Geopolitical Tensions
events.description: The International Monetary Fund upgraded its global growth outlook despite concerns over a more persistent energy market disruption than anticipated due to tensions in the Middle East. In the World Economic Outlook, released Tuesday, the IMF lifted its global growth outlook for this year to 3.1 percent from 3.0 percent estimated in July. But this was weaker than the 3.5 percent growth in 2025.

events.title: Yen Rises After BoJ Ueda Comments
events.description: The Japanese yen strengthened against other major currencies in the late European session on Tuesday, after the Bank of Japan or the BoJ Governor Kazuho Ueda's comments left the door open to further interest rate hikes.

events.title: Yen Rises Against Majors
events.description: The Japanese yen strengthened against other major currencies in the late European session on Tuesday.

events.title: Bay Street May Open Higher; Tech Stocks Likely To Decline
events.description: Canadian stocks are seen opening on a positive note Tuesday morning, tracking higher gold prices and on easing worries about inflation following a sharp drop in oil prices. Tech stocks may find the going a bit tough amid renewed uncertainty about returns on AI investments.

events.title: FTSE 100 Rises 0.65% As Oil Prices Fall On Russia Export Lift
events.description: UK stocks climbed for a third consecutive session Tuesday, with the FTSE 100 gaining 0.65% to 10,725.98. Easing oil prices and bond yields supported sentiment, while Brent crude fell 1.7% to $104.90 a barrel as Russia partially lifted diesel export restrictions.

events.title: Johnson & Johnson Q3 Profit Plunges, Lifts FY26 Outlook; Stock Drops
events.description: Drug major Johnson & Johnson on Tuesday reported sharply lower third-quarter profit on special charges, despite sales growth. Further, the firm raised its fiscal 2026 outlook again and announced a quarterly dividend. In pre-market activity, the shares were losing around 2.6 percent.
